messages:
maria: Quick follow-up to last week's RFC — I'm leaning toward a split control plane model for Private deployments: a customer-owned control plane (VPC-hosted control plane components + PrivateLink/NLB endpoints) for high-compliance customers, and a shared hosted control plane for hosted/dedicated customers. Need feedback on interface boundaries and peering patterns.

kevin: are we talking full control-plane separation (no shared metadata services at all) or just the traffic plane?

maria: full-ish — control plane APIs (model catalog, rollout manager, auth) would be reachable only from the customer VPC via private endpoints. Shared control plane would still exist for typical customers, but it must be functionally identical.

jess: main tradeoffs I see: cert/key provisioning per customer, DNS & discovery, and ops surface area. Also peering scale: VPC peering vs Transit Gateway vs PrivateLink.

samir: +1. VPC peering -> easy routing semantics but hits route table limits and cross-account trust. Transit Gateway solves scale but is more expensive and adds a single central point to manage. PrivateLink gives strong isolation but requires endpoint services per region/per-AZ.

alan: Another angle: offer two interface options: 1) customer-managed endpoints (they create NLBs & we talk to them over mutual TLS) and 2) provider-managed private endpoints (we create privatelink endpoints into their account). That avoids cross-account peering for high-security customers.

maria: that's what I was thinking. For customer-managed endpoints we require an IP allowlist + mTLS + customer-provided cert fingerprint. For provider-managed PrivateLink we'll provision ENIs in their account and manage endpoint services on our side.

kevin: how do we handle auth tokens and API versioning boundary? If control plane is customer-owned, we still need a standard API contract. Do we require them to run a tiny control-plane shim that implements our contract?

jess: yes — a lightweight shim (signed by us) that implements auth validation, schema checks, and forwards to local control-plane components. That gives us a stable API contract while allowing local hosting.

samir: rollout concerns: we need a migration path for existing customers using shared CP. Could do phased opt-in: beta -> opt-in per-customer -> cutover window with webhook-based readiness checks. Also need to surface metrics to our console from customer CPs.

alan: on DNS: split-horizon DNS per-customer is messy. Simpler: use stable service hostnames and issue customer-specific SRV records or use ALB/NLB CNAMEs the customer places into their DNS. PrivateLink avoids DNS headaches since VPC DNS resolves the endpoint automatically.

maria: notes on encryption/key mgmt: for provider-managed endpoints we store & rotate endpoint certs in our KMS and push them via the provisioning flow. For customer-managed endpoints we require their KMS-backed certs and we validate via CT logs + fingerprint.

kevin: operational: who owns upgrades for the customer control plane? If customer-managed endpoints + our shim, we can push shim updates automatically but the rest should be in their control. We need an emergency rollback path if an update breaks compatibility.

jess: add an HTTP/health + /compat-check endpoint to the shim that the control plane can call during rollouts. Also add canary toggles on our side to route small % of traffic to the new control-plane variant.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new design will require infra changes: TGW peering role, privatelink svc infra, cross-account IAM delegate role, and a new provisioning lambda.

samir: monitoring & billing: ensure token-level attribution still works when CP is customer-hosted. We should require a forwarding of event logs to our telemetry endpoint (signed) and fall back to per-request attestation headers.

alan: we must avoid lateral network access from the customer CP into our core infra. Only allow the specific API endpoints and metrics egress to our ingestion plane. Network policies + Egress NAT + VPC endpoint policies.

maria: open questions for the RFC follow-up: 1) which option is default for enterprise customers? 2) exact provisioning flow for provider-managed PrivateLink (permissions + auditing). 3) shim contract + versioning rules. 4) SLA implications and support boundaries.

kevin: my vote: default = provider-managed PrivateLink for enterprise, opt-in customer-managed endpoints for the highest-compliance customers. Leaves room for Transit Gateway offerings later.

jess: agreed. I'll draft the shim API contract and a minimal terraform example for customer-managed NLB + route table entries.

maria: thanks — please drop comments in the RFC doc and I'll synthesize. tl;dr: hybrid split-control-plane, provider-managed PrivateLink as default enterprise pattern, customer-managed for exceptional cases. :+1:

alan: one more thing — add a kill-switch we can trigger remotely to disable a customer CP if we detect abuse. Need legal + support alignment.

maria: good catch. will add to security & compliance section.

kevin: small example route snippet we'd need (customer-managed NLB path):
```
# customer route table (example)
route:
  destination_cidr_block: 10.20.0.0/24
  target: eni-xxxxxxx # NLB ENI
```

jess: starting the shim doc now. will ping when first draft is ready.

maria: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the canonical follow-up for the RFC. If anyone wants to pair on the provisioning automation ping me.
